transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-29
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Jordan Patel (Redwood); Sam Ruiz, Priya Kapoor, Liam O'Neill, Hana Park (AuroraSense)

Summary:
Quick re-check after the incident last week where AuroraSense saw long-tail stalls and eviction waves at peak. Goal: align on mitigation path (short-term compensating controls + pilot for Dedicated capacity), confirm security/compliance checklist for Private and get sample traffic for repro.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Sam Ruiz: yep, loud and clear, thanks Maya. we wanted to get a short follow up, try to get a concrete plan, not just high level things.
[00:12] Maya Chen: totally. Jordan from our SE team is here to dig into the traces. brief agenda: 1) what we saw, 2) quick mitigations, 3) pilot scope for dedicated/private, 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: yes, please. also a reminder our CISO asked for KMS integration notes and a short SOC2 appendix.
[00:28] Jordan Patel: noted; we'll share those. quick note on naming — when I say "KV cache" that's our local LLM prefix cache, sometimes might be spoken as KV-store in our notes.

[02:01] Jordan Patel: ok so from Redwood side, the incident looked like repeated long-prefix evictions correlated with bursty traffic at ~t0 14:11 UTC last Tuesday. we saw the KV cache load spike and the inference runtime started backfilling kms — sorry, not kms, kv — backfilling KV cache which pushed CPU across nodes and caused token generation stalls.
[02:25] Sam Ruiz: interrupt — when you say backfilling, is that the prefetch we talked about or full reconstruction?
[02:30] Jordan Patel: it's reconstruction of the cached key/value entries for a given session; the cache eviction policy was tuned for avg path, not the heavy tail of your prompt sizes, so when you have a mix of long dialogues plus lots of short inference, the memory pressure nudge caused frequent full reconstructions.
[02:48] Priya Kapoor: that matches our logs, we saw many recon structs and a lot of CPU spindle. the tail latency grew to >10s for some requests.

[05:10] Maya Chen: ok so there are three buckets for mitigation: immediate (config + routing), near-term (Dedicated pilot + quantization profile) and long-term (runtime kernel tweaks and improved eviction heuristics).
[05:28] Hana Park: can you explain the routing option?
[05:32] Jordan Patel: sure — smart routing is a policy layer where we can route heavy long-sequence requests to a Dedicated pool with larger KV capacity or to a model variant with shorter context, and route short requests to a cheaper, higher throughput pool. it reduces cross-traffic noise. but it needs canarying because the model variant may change semantics slightly.
[05:53] Liam O'Neill: during the outage we also hit our quota limits on shared hosted and had degraded fallback behaviour, is Dedicated guaranteed to avoid that?
[06:02] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and controlled autoscaling policies; it won't jam because of noisy tenants. SLA-wise we can provide latency targets and also a throttled burst window that you can configure.

[07:30] Jordan Patel: i want to highlight a weird bit — some of the transcripts show inaccurate model labels, e.g., some calls reference "Redwood Lite" which was our shorthand; in logs it appears as red-llm-lite. the mismatch made our oncall triage slower. it's a small housekeeping item but worth clarifying in the pilot.

[09:00] Priya Kapoor: our security team flagged KMS rotation and HSM compatibility for the Private option — we need to know if Redwood supports external HSM, and what's the key tenancy model.
[09:12] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and can be configured for customer-managed keys via HSM; Jordan will share the architecture note and the SOC2 appendix.

[12:40] Jordan Patel: ok walking through traces — i'm going to paste a couple of short snippets: at 14:11:34 there is a spike in open sessions followed by a cascade of eviction events. cache miss rate jumps from 4%->38% within 20s. as misses increase, backfill work is scheduled on the GPU CPU host, we see scheduling latencies climb and token generation stalls. there's also a minor memory leak in an older runtime path that exacerbated the pressure — we patched that last week but hadn't rolled the fix to all clusters yet.
[13:15] Sam Ruiz: is that leak what's causing the gradual degradation across the hour?
[13:20] Jordan Patel: partly. the leak alone would cause slow drift, but the eviction cascade was the trigger due to your workload mix and momentary spike.

[16:00] Maya Chen: immediate actions we propose: 1) apply a conservative KV cache size bump for AuroraSense on the hosted pool (fast change), 2) enable per-customer routing for long contexts to a reserved node pool (quick feature flip), 3) deploy our fallback tuning so that requests above 4s get a faster 1-pass fallback policy. these should reduce 95/99th latencies within the hour of change.
[16:35] Priya Kapoor: what's the runtime risk for the fast change? can we rollback?
[16:40] Jordan Patel: it's reversible — it's a config toggle. we'll push in canary and monitor traces; rollback is immediate.

[20:10] Liam O'Neill: for canarying, we want transparent tracing — request ids, per-token timing, and cache hit annotations in the trace. can Redwood expose traces into our datadog?
[20:22] Maya Chen: yes, we can forward traces and provide an opentelemetry hook. Jordan will include the example config.

[23:45] Sam Ruiz: cost question — if we route long contexts to Dedicated, what's the expected delta in USD per 1M tokens?
[23:54] Maya Chen: rough ballpark depends on GPU type; Dedicated reduces cross-tenant inefficiencies so unit cost often drops, but because it's reserved, your fixed cost increases. we'll send a tailored estimate after we see your traffic histogram.

[27:00] Jordan Patel: near-term steps for stability: set up a Dedicated pool with slightly larger KV allocation, apply our quantization profile for your model family (we have validated q4_0 and q5-lite for comparable latency) and run a controlled load test. also, we'll run a 2-hour eviction-wave repro in our lab using your sample prompts to validate heuristics.

[30:10] Hana Park: regarding the repro, can you replay TLS-encrypted payloads or do we need to strip anything?
[30:18] Jordan Patel: we accept sanitized prompt sets; we don't need the encrypted envelope. please remove PII. we want shape and timing, not real data.

[34:00] Priya Kapoor: long-term, you mentioned kernel changes and eviction heuristic improvements. how long until those are available?
[34:08] Jordan Patel: kernel-level optimizations are in active dev — likely Q3 for a staged rollout. eviction heuristics can be tuned much faster; we can push heuristic changes in weeks. full runtime kernel work takes more validation because of hardware matrix.

[36:45] Maya Chen: an important compliance note: if you choose Private with customer-managed KMS, there's an onboarding checklist — SSO/SAML metadata, RBAC roles, network CIDR ranges, and audit log destination. Liam, you mentioned RBAC scope — can you jot down which teams need admin vs read-only?
[36:58] Liam O'Neill: yes we'll send that after this call.

[40:20] Sam Ruiz: any competitive risk if we move to Dedicated? NimbusAI keeps pitching single-tenant endpoints with guaranteed tail SLOs.
[40:28] Maya Chen: we know NimbusAI — they are single-tenant but often tradeoff observability and model flexibility. Redwood offers unified routing, rollouts, and better tooling for multi-environment parity — we can demonstrate parity in a pilot.

[44:00] Jordan Patel: recording some low-confidence transcriptions we saw in the incident ticket: "prefetch path" got transcribed as "pre-fetch bath", "eviction wave" sometimes came out as "aviction"; small things but they mattered for search. we'll normalize naming in the runbook.

[47:30] Priya Kapoor: ok let's go through the concrete schedule — we want the eviction repro and traces before the pilot. and the pilot gating checks are: 1) repro shows <10% tail amplification, 2) RBAC & SSO tested in staging, 3) security docs in place.

[49:05] Maya Chen: agreed. Jordan will run repro and attach traces, Maya will send security appendix + estimate, and we will propose pilot dates.

[52:10] Hana Park: any other actions on our side besides prompts and RBAC?
[52:18] Liam O'Neill: we'll also collect a rolling 24h histogram with 1s granularity for request interarrival times and token lengths — that'll help with batching heuristics.

[55:40] Maya Chen: great. recap of next steps briefly — send prompt set and histogram, Redwood runs repro and shares traces and config diff, Redwood shares KMS/HSM integration notes and SOC2 appendix, propose pilot week.
[56:05] Sam Ruiz: thanks, that sounds good. one last ask — can we get a short 1-page emergency playbook for our oncall folks to follow if this happens again?
[56:14] Jordan Patel: yes, we have a playbook template; we'll tailor it and share.
[56:20] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the scheduling options.
[56:27] Sam Ruiz: great, thanks all.

End of transcript.

References: runbook link (to be shared), SOC2 appendix (to be attached), KMS integration note (to be attached).

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings and product nickname mismatches; please rely on attached traces for exact timings.
